quotes.text: I would rather see the electric cars of the future, the digital currencies of the future, built and regulated by the United States, not China.

Ultimately, the United States will need a clear national framework for AI governance — one that protects safety, privacy and transparency while still encouraging innovation. A patchwork of state-by-state rules will not be enough for a technology that operates across borders and affects every American community.

Technology companies should play an important role in building safeguards, especially for young people. But we cannot rely on them alone. Artificial intelligence is advancing too quickly and shaping too many parts of our economy and society to leave its rules entirely to private companies.

Artificial intelligence is changing the future our students are stepping into. We need to make sure every child in Utah is prepared to succeed in it. I recently wrote an opinion piece for the Deseret News discussing steps we can take today to address this rapidly growing technology.

https://t.co/qMLcRUxxXN

I do believe that technology and the AI fight is going to be a central part of America's and Utah's future, and it's critical that our leaders understand this space and ensure growth happens in the right way.

Artificial intelligence is going to transform our economy in some good ways and in many bad ways. What we need are federal standards to make sure that when, as the economy is transformed, that the American people are the ones who benefit, not tech billionaires, tech moguls, foreign powers, but the American people are benefited through that.

I would start by saying if we could put the genie back in the bottle, I would do that. [...] We see oligarchs that are profiting from the system at the expense of everybody else, and that can't be the case. We have to see that this transformative technology is lifting everyday Utahns, and we need to have standards in place that protect our air quality and protect the Great Salt Lake.

And then looking more broadly at AI, I think this is a transformative technology. It's going to cure diseases, prolong human life, enhance quality of life, but we have to be at the forefront of making sure that's done responsibly and that it lifts everybody, not just enriches a few.

I just finished a CD1 candidate forum. The first question was about AI. Here’s what I think. 

AI is coming. It’s up to every member of Congress to be proactive in providing oversight of this industry in order to protect jobs, our kids, the environment, and the fabric of our communities. That will require federal guardrails to make sure this technology happens carefully and transparently, with appropriate regulation, strong oversight, human accountability, and safeguards for data privacy and civil rights.

AI could potentially cure cancer, but it could also destroy our kids. I believe thoughtful policy can unleash the good and stop the bad.

Look, anytime the makers of AI are talking about a 10% risk of annihilation of humanity, I think that's something we should take pretty serious. But I will tell you, and the federal government and this administration has not taken it seriously, and Congress has not done its job.

But I'll tell you what else, is we have 100% certainty that AI will transform and disrupt our economy. [...] And this is a time where we need to decide, this is a choice that will be made, who's gonna benefit from this disruptive technology, tech bros and billionaires?

This is something that's gonna be hard to regulate on a 50-state basis, or, you know, we need a strong federal standard, strong federal guardrails that are gonna protect us from the harms of AI and make sure that any economic disruption does not hurt the American people, does not result in the enriching of billionaires and trillionaires, but helps to lift every American.

Every election year, I look forward to visiting our senior centers for Salt Lake County’s Candidate Days.

Most of what I heard came back to one idea: people did everything they were supposed to do. They worked, they paid into Social Security and Medicare every paycheck, and they planned for a fixed income. Now they’re the ones absorbing the costs. Higher prices on prescriptions. Property taxes climbing on houses they’ve owned for 40 years. And a scam call or text nearly every day, getting harder to spot as AI advances.

In Congress, I’ll protect the Social Security and Medicare benefits people earned and fight any cuts to them. I’ll keep pushing for property tax relief so seniors can stay in their homes, and I’ll go after the scammers targeting older Utahns.

Thank you to Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services for putting these days together, and to everyone who sat down and talked with us.
